note: The section is `swin`, not a `section.board`: the mock models Settings as
<div class="swin" id="swin" data-state="ideal" role="dialog"> at :1513. mock-affordances.py
matches any element by id, so no engine change was needed for that.
FOUR DECLARED DIVERGENCES. A finding outside this list is a defect; a finding inside it is a
difference with an owner and a number attached, which is what this gate is for.
1. THE SOURCE LIST IS 256pt AND THE MOCK DRAWS 200. Not "we could not derive 200". A settings
source list is a sidebar, DESIGN.md §2 specifies `Sidebar 256pt`, MetricToken.sidebar is that
value, and the mock's own mac-craft:metrics block carries `sidebar 256px` and no 200 of any
name — so the mock disagrees with itself as well as with the document.
DesignTokenParityTests compares MetricToken's name set against §2's table for exact equality
in both directions, so a `settingsSidebar` case without a new §2 row reddens it, and
authoring that row is M21's substance. Owner: M21.
2. FOUR OF THE SEVEN SOURCE-LIST SYMBOLS HAVE NO Icon CASE. The mock draws #i-servers,
#i-harness, #i-bolt, #i-download, #i-shield, #i-menubar and #i-sliders; Icon carries servers,
bolt and shield exactly and has no harness, download, menubar or sliders. Its count is
asserted as spriteSymbols (21) + drawnReplacementsForUnicode (1) against THE PROTOTYPE's
sprite in DesignSystemTests, so adding four cases re-bases that inventory from one document
to the other. The panes reuse layers, tray, list and settings instead. Owner: M21.
3. THE MOCK IS A TAB SET AND THE BUILD IS A SPLIT VIEW. All seven panes sit in the mock's DOM
at once with `.active` deciding which is visible, so `v-ideal` inventories all seven panes'
contents; a NavigationSplitView detail renders the selected pane and nothing else. Six of the
seven panes are therefore absent from any one run. This is a difference in how the surface is
modelled, not a missing control, and it is why the absent count here is large. Owner: nobody
— it is the conversion, and closing it would mean rendering seven panes at once.
4. THIRTEEN OF THE MOCK'S THIRTY ROWS NAME CAPABILITIES THIS PRODUCT DOES NOT HAVE. spec-M15
§2's fifth assumption forbids building a control for one. Every such row carries the
pre-existing artifact that recorded the absence in settings.pairing.tsv. Owner: whichever
item builds the capability; the row becomes buildable then and not before.
`loading` and `error` are OMITTED FROM states AND INVENTORIED HERE rather than dropped in
silence, which is M23's A6 precedent. spec-M15 §2's ninth assumption gives the panes' loading
and error wording to M17; listing them here without building them would make every run exit 1
on absent affordances, which reports a scope boundary as a defect. Owner: M17.
THE FLOORS ARE RECORDED, NOT CHOSEN, and that is the mechanism rather than a hole in it. They
are the census sizes measured on the first run whose structure layer was clean, they only ever
rise, and Context.__init__ exits 3 for a floor below 1 or non-integer. A floor lowered later to
make a run green is the failure this shape has to be watched for: a shrunken denominator raises
reported coverage while measuring less, which planning/evidence/P4-acceptance.md records four
separate times.

layers.name: font-weight-face
layers.substitute: A SwiftUI Font is opaque — String(describing: Font.system(size: 13, weight: .semibold)) returns "Font(provider: SwiftUI.FontBox<SwiftUI.Font.SystemProvider>)", with no size, weight or face in it. Confirmed instead by: the TypeToken each text node names is recorded in tokens["type"] at apply time and checked against the measured line box by the type-metrics layer; DesignTokenParityTests pins the eight-role ladder against DESIGN.md; scripts/lint/no-raw-design-values.sh fails any font size that does not come off it. None of the three can see an ancestor .font() winning the cascade, and that residue is what this row is.
